heading: Good Standing
text: For undergraduate good academic standing, PSU requires a term GPA of at least 2.25 and a cumulative PSU GPA of at least 2.00.

heading: Academic Warning and Improving Academic Standing
text: A student on academic warning who raises the term GPA to at least 2.25 but has a cumulative PSU GPA below 2.00 remains on warning. Returning to good standing requires bringing the cumulative PSU GPA to 2.00 or above.

heading: Academic Warning Credit Limit
text: Students placed on academic warning are limited to 13 credits in future terms unless an academic advisor approves taking more.

heading: Repeat Policy Scope
text: This undergraduate repeat policy applies to duplicate courses. When the first attempt earned a C-range or higher grade, that first grade remains included in the GPA calculation.

heading: Eligible Repeat Grades
text: When an undergraduate first earns D+, D, D-, or F in a PSU course, repeats that course at PSU using a letter grade (not Pass/No-Pass), and completes the required repeated-course notice, the first low grade may be excluded from the GPA calculation. Both grades stay on the transcript.

heading: Repeated Course Notice
text: PSU requires submission of a Notice of Repeated Course form for the initial D/F-grade exclusion to be reflected in the official GPA.

heading: Pass Grades
text: At PSU, a Pass (P) grade gives course credit but does not enter the GPA calculation. A passing grade generally corresponds to C- or higher for undergraduates and B- or higher for graduates, though departments can differ.

heading: Auditing Courses
text: An audited course earns no degree credit, does not count toward degree requirements, and is not included in the GPA. Normal tuition and fees still apply.

heading: Grading Options
text: Some PSU courses offer both letter grades and Pass/No Pass; others permit only one grading mode.

heading: Undergraduate Pass Credit Limits
text: Up to 45 Pass credits can be applied toward a bachelor’s degree, but no more than 20 of the final 45 PSU credits may have Pass grades. Many majors also require letter-graded courses.

heading: Pass Credit for Prerequisites
text: Pass credits generally cannot satisfy prerequisites unless the relevant department approves an exception.

heading: Graduate Program Restrictions
text: For graduate degrees, PSU does not set a universal upper limit on Pass-graded courses, but individual graduate programs may set tighter rules.

heading: Regular-Term Tuition Refund Schedule
text: For regular fall, winter, and spring terms, PSU lists tuition refunds by week as follows: first week 100%, second week 70%, third week 40%, fourth week 20%, and fifth week 0%. Summer follows a different schedule.

heading: Drop Charges and Account Adjustments
text: Dropping after the first week can trigger a drop charge as well as a partial tuition refund. Other university balances may be paid from money otherwise due as a refund, and student aid refunds have additional rules.

heading: Refund Disbursement
text: A published tuition-refund percentage does not by itself determine the amount or timing of a particular student’s bank deposit. The student’s account obligations, charges, and refund delivery option also affect the outcome.

heading: Pre-Term Waitlist Notification
text: Being on a PSU course waitlist does not cause automatic registration when a space opens. Before the term, PSU emails the student, who then has exactly 24 hours to claim the seat by following registration instructions. If not registered in time, the student loses the waitlist position.

heading: Waitlists After Term Begins
text: After the term starts, automatic waitlist notifications stop. Students need instructor permission to register; instructors can give approval but cannot enroll students directly.

heading: Closed Classes Without Waitlists
text: For a closed class with no waitlist, PSU says a student may still be added through instructor or department approval documented on a Special Registration Form.

heading: Waitlist Availability
text: A closed course only provides waitlist access when the department has enabled a waitlist and it has space. If there is no waitlist or the waitlist is full, the registration section is closed to waitlisting.

heading: Override Approval
text: PSU describes electronic overrides and approval procedures for restricted or full classes; students may seek an override through the indicated processes.

heading: Federal Work Study Enrollment
text: PSU states that Federal Work Study requires at least half-time enrollment, meaning six or more credits. Withdrawal can affect whether a student may continue working during that term.

heading: Impact of Withdrawal
text: The PSU guidance says work-study eligibility may change after withdrawal.

heading: Financial Aid Appeals
text: Financial aid appeals can be used to seek conditional aid eligibility for a future term. The published guidance does not allow an appeal of financial aid eligibility for a previous term that has already ended.
